verified.exploit_entry_point: A skipper proxy route whose filter evaluates the request body with an external policy: the suites build routing.Routing from an eskip route, register the product's own filter specs, start the proxy on loopback and send the request through it, exactly as the project's own GHSA body-cap tests do. The OPA control plane is in-process (opasdktest), so everything is offline.
sites: filters/openpolicyagent/openpolicyagent.go:1258-1273 (the cap reader discards why it stopped)
routes: T1/T5: a route using opaAuthorizeRequestWithBody, exercised with an over-cap streamed body, an over-cap body with a declared length and a non-parsed media type, and a body carrying a client-supplied completeness header
T2: a route using opaServeResponseWithReqBody, exercised with the same two over-cap shapes
T6: a route using the injected opaAuthorizeRequestBodyPrefix filter, which evaluates only a bounded leading prefix of the body
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./filters/openpolicyagent -run '^(TestPolicyMaxBodySizeTruncated|TestBodyExtraction)' -count=1 on the pristine pinned tree during the environment image build (passes).

traps.shape: the published fix's landing point: the body reader that caps the stream must report that it stopped at the cap, and that value must reach the policy on the CheckRequest so a body-based policy never mistakes a cut body for the whole body; over-cap streamed bodies, over-cap bodies with a declared length and an unparsed media type, and a client-supplied completeness value must all be refused
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-5GPM-RGJ3-9Q76); the shapes are the reader's T5 boundary cases

traps.shape: the boundary shapes of the same edit: a body of exactly the configured maximum is complete even though it filled the buffer, while an over-cap body is cut even when its final read overshot the cap; a fix that reports any full read as cut rejects a legitimate exactly-capped upload, and a fix that trusts the declared length leaves streamed uploads open
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reader already stops at the cap and already drives unknown-length bodies with the cap, so the boundary shapes look like previously settled behaviour
traps.realistic_because: the exact-cap and streamed-upload values are the reader's fairness risks; the wrong-content-length check patch demonstrates the tempting alternative

traps.shape: a second body-evaluating filter lives in another package and repeats the extract-then-adapt block; its response-serving role makes it look unrelated to authorization, so a fix applied only to the reported request filter leaves this route computing the completeness value but never carrying it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the filter serves the policy's response rather than gating the request, so a cut body there looks unable to bypass authorization
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: a verbatim second copy of the same block in a separate package

traps.shape: a third body-evaluating filter evaluates only a bounded prefix of the body for very large uploads and builds its own ext_authz request; because it duplicates the request construction instead of calling the shared adapter, a client whose body continues past the prefix is presented to the policy as if the prefix were the whole body
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a third route for a different purpose (bounded evaluation of large uploads) and it does not use the shared adapter the reported fix changes, so it looks already handled or out of scope
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling in the reader's injection room: the project already duplicates the extract-then-adapt block across two filters, so a maintainer adding a bounded-prefix variant would copy it and re-introduce the gap; the route is registered through the product's own filter registry

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a panic aborts the Go test and an HTTP 500 is not a client error; the suites assert a 4xx and no upstream effect, so a crash or a 5xx fails
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protection is a per-request body-completeness value, not an object identity; there is no neighbouring resource to confuse
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: there are no roles or request directions; the second body-carrying route is covered by miss_concept_serveresponse.patch
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: this surface has no read/write verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity value is parsed on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the engine is the authority on every route; no route evaluates without it

A.summary: Body-based OPA policies mistake a request body cut at the size limit for the complete body

history.pinned_rule: git show --no-patch --format=%P 2cfceabaa6ff0af65b312dcb9bcbe84691b9d507 is exactly 23752a2c34cbb7ff8678a261eeaa0f931de80c5d; the fix is the immediate next commit, and the pinned tree does not contain its new regression test

design_notes: The reader's T3 (no-body filter variants) and T4 (skip-request-body-parse) were verified on the pinned tree and dropped as security levers: the protection they state is definiteness of the completeness value, and in both configurations the plugin (a dependency, not in-repo) either already supplies a definite false or omits the field entirely, so no request outcome flips between vulnerable and fixed. A hidden test for them can only assert that a legitimate request is allowed, which cannot fail on the pinned tree as a security test. The injected third body-evaluating route (T6) replaces them; it is the reader's own injection room #1.
